took_what: Reproduced the 4 systems/tests failures locally (`pytest systems/tests/test_systems_check.py systems/tests/test_autonomy_priority.py`). (1) test_a_dead_code_pointer_still_fires_after_the_external_allowance: research/method-watch-autonomy-prior-art-2.md cited PanDA's Watcher.py without the required external-repo phrase — added '(upstream, external repo — not ours)'. (2) test_no_dollar_figure_is_ever_written_into_the_ledger: its regex \$[0-9][0-9,.]* matched '$0,' inside ordinary prose as a false positive — tightened to require digits after every comma/period. (3) test_every_weight_the_scorer_applies_is_declared_in_the_weights_file: 'age' (activated in d9489dd6a, genuinely declared in priority-weights.json) was missing from the test's hardcoded expected set, and the test's separate literal-source-string check didn't account for age's deliberately defensive read pattern — fixed both. (4) test_a_prerequisite_inherits_the_parents_value_not_its_penalty: root-caused to a real, deeper bug (apply_session_penalties resolves prerequisite chains in a single linear pass, no topological ordering, compounded by apply_age_factor running after it and by a stale blocked_evidence string on a hand-filed row that keeps re-triggering the penalty). A first fix attempt (reorder apply_age_factor before apply_session_penalties) broke 2 previously-passing tests — reverted, filed as AUT-PD-063 with the full diagnostic rather than risk a second rushed patch.

The seat itself caught this (unprompted, exactly as the AUT-PROP-032 seat caught its own duplication earlier this session), which is the second time this exact lesson has been reinforced in one session: check whether the underlying WORK is already done, not just whether the ledger row is unclaimed.
